tree.name: img_2
tree.rationale: Since the reported metrics are recall@k (objective says maximize) and the CLIP-median filter lowered every recall, test the mildest standard signal alone — drop near-duplicates (~84.5k rows) — to isolate whether dedup helps without the diversity loss that aggressive CLIP filtering caused.

tree.name: img_3
tree.rationale: CLIP-based quality filtering hurt and dedup was neutral, so test an orthogonal signal — drop tiny/thumbnail-sized images (likely upscaled or junk, ~65k rows remain) — to see if low-resolution noise is what limits retrieval recall.

tree.name: img_5
tree.rationale: CLIP, resolution, and dedup filters were neutral-to-harmful, so test the one untested signal alone — keep the top half by `similarity` (~50k rows) — to see whether it carries different information than CLIP score.

tree.name: img_1
tree.rationale: Test the single strongest known curation signal—CLIP image-text alignment—by keeping the top 50% (~50k rows, well above min_rows) before layering in dedup or aesthetic filters.

tree.name: img_4
tree.rationale: CLIP thresholding gave the biggest gain so far, so test whether pushing it from the top-50% to the top-25% (~25k rows, still above min_rows) improves score further before combining signals.
